# File

An owned, open file.

```rux
pub struct File {
    // private fields
}
```

Move-only: the handle closes exactly once, through [`Close`](/docs/api/filesystem/file#close) or through its destructor. [`Close`](/docs/api/filesystem/file#close) is the
error-visible path; destruction discards the outcome, which is fine for a file that was read and a silent
loss for one that was written.

## Associated functions

<h3 id="open"><code>Open</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Open(allocator: Allocator, path: Path, options: OpenOptions) -> File ! IoError
```

Opens `path` under `options`.
The allocator is borrowed for the platform form of the path and holds nothing afterward. A failure says why
in the platform's own terms, translated.

| Name        | Type          | Description                                                    |
| ----------- | ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `allocator` | `Allocator`   | where the storage comes from                                   |
| `path`      | `Path`        | the path to act on                                             |
| `options`   | `OpenOptions` | what may be done with the file, and what to do about existence |

**Returns**: the open file

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/FileSystem/Src/File.rux#L165)

## Methods

<h3 id="is-open"><code>IsOpen</code></h3>

```rux
pub func IsOpen(self: &File) -> bool
```

Whether the handle is still open.

**Returns**: whether the file is open

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/FileSystem/Src/File.rux#L234)

<h3 id="close"><code>Close</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Close(self: &var File) -> ! IoError
```

Closes the handle and reports what the platform said.
Closing twice is not an error here: the second call is a no-op reporting success, because the first already
gave the handle back. This is the error-visible path; a written file deserves it.

**Returns**: success when the descriptor was released; closing twice is not an error

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/FileSystem/Src/File.rux#L243)

<h3 id="sync"><code>Sync</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Sync(self: &var File) -> ! IoError
```

Forces everything written through to the storage device.
Not "handed to the kernel" but "acknowledged by the device": the promise that holds through a power
failure, and the one a caller who just wrote something they cannot lose actually wants.

**Returns**: success when the system reported the data durable

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/FileSystem/Src/File.rux#L125)

<h3 id="size"><code>Size</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Size(self: &var File) -> uint64 ! IoError
```

The file's length in bytes.
On the Unix systems this is measured by seeking to the end and back, which moves the shared kernel
position for a moment; a reader racing this on the same open file may see it. The stat-based answer
arrives with the metadata work.

**Returns**: the file's size in bytes

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/FileSystem/Src/File.rux#L142)

<h3 id="set-length"><code>SetLength</code></h3>

```rux
pub func SetLength(self: &var File, length: uint64) -> ! IoError
```

Sets the file's length: shrinking discards what was past the new end, growing leaves a hole.
The position does not move. A position past the new end stays where it was, and the next write there
grows the file again — the same rule as seeking past the end.

| Name     | Type     | Description                              |
| -------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `length` | `uint64` | the size the file should have afterwards |

**Returns**: success when the file is that size; extending reads back as zeros

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/FileSystem/Src/File.rux#L166)

<h3 id="stream"><code>Stream</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Stream(self: *var File) -> FileStream
```

A stored borrow of this file, for a value that must keep a stream beyond one call.
For anything that only needs a stream for the duration of a call, borrow the file directly as
`let sink: &var Writer = file;` instead: that is checked, and this is not.
The file must outlive the result and must not be moved while it exists. See [`FileStream`](/docs/api/filesystem/file-stream).

**Returns**: a stream over this file, holding its address, which is what makes it storable

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/FileSystem/Src/File.rux#L195)

<h3 id="metadata"><code>Metadata</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Metadata(self: &File) -> Metadata ! IoError
```

Describes this open file.
Answers about the file the handle holds, so nothing can rename or replace the name out from under the
query the way a path-based one can.

**Returns**: what the system knows about the open file

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/FileSystem/Src/File.rux#L391)

<h3 id="flush"><code>Flush</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Flush(self: &var File) -> ! IoError
```

Nothing: these writes hold nothing back. Durability is [`Sync`](/docs/api/filesystem/file#sync), which is a different promise.

**Returns**: success when everything written reached the system

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/FileSystem/Src/File.rux#L81)

## Implements Seeker

`File` conforms to `Seeker`.

<h3 id="seek"><code>Seek</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Seek(self: &var File, origin: SeekFrom, offset: int64) -> uint64 ! IoError
```

Moves the position `offset` bytes from `origin` and reports where it landed.
A position before the start of the file is refused by the platform; one past the end is allowed, and a
later write there leaves a hole. A handle opened for appending still seeks — but its writes land at the
end regardless, because append is a property of the writes, not of the position.

| Name     | Type       | Description                       |
| -------- | ---------- | --------------------------------- |
| `origin` | `SeekFrom` | where the offset is measured from |
| `offset` | `int64`    | how far to move                   |

**Returns**: the resulting offset from the start

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/FileSystem/Src/File.rux#L95)

## Related

<h3 id="open-options"><code>OpenOptions</code></h3>

```rux
pub struct OpenOptions {
    pub write: bool;
    pub truncate: bool;
    pub create: bool;
    pub createNew: bool;
    // private fields
}
```

What an open may do, and what it does about existence.
`read`, `write` and `append` say what may happen through the handle; `create`, `createNew` and `truncate` say
what happens to the file itself. `append` positions every write at the end, whatever was written in between,
which is the property log writers need and `write` alone does not have.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/FileSystem/Src/File.rux#L41)

**Fields**

| Name        | Type   | Description                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ----------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `write`     | `bool` | The handle may write.                                                                                                                                                                |
| `truncate`  | `bool` | An existing file's contents are discarded on open. Requires `write`.                                                                                                                 |
| `create`    | `bool` | A missing file is created. Requires `write` or `append`.                                                                                                                             |
| `createNew` | `bool` | The file must not exist: it is created, and an existing one is `AlreadyExists`. Wins over `create` and `truncate`, and is the option that makes creation a claim rather than a race. |
